implementation_notes: asyncio.TaskGroup (3.11+) is the structural-concurrency realization: one tg.create_task(deliver(r, copy)) per recipient and the async with block awaits them all on exit, cancelling the siblings when one delivery raises. asyncio.gather(*coros, return_exceptions=True) is the older, continue-on-error form that reports per-recipient outcomes, and Celery/Kombu are only needed when delivery must survive a process restart. Both asyncio forms replace the router component; what remains yours is the recipient computation and the decision between fail-fast and continue.
code_sketch:
async def fan_out(msg: Message, recipients: list[Recipient]) -> None:
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:        # Python 3.11+
        for r in recipients:                     # runtime-computed recipient set
            tg.create_task(r.deliver(copy.deepcopy(msg)))   # own copy per recipient
    # exiting the block awaits every task and cancels the rest on first failure
pitfalls: A failing delivery is wrapped in an ExceptionGroup, so callers need except* (or gather(return_exceptions=True)) to see per-recipient outcomes rather than one aggregated crash.
asyncio.create_task holds only a weak reference: a fire-and-forget send that is not stored can be garbage-collected mid-flight.
A synchronous blocking client (requests, pika) inside a task blocks the whole event loop for every recipient; use the async client or run_in_executor.

variants.name: Celery broker fan-out (durable, cross-process)
variants.implementation_notes: When the recipients are remote workers and the fan-out must survive a restart, each recipient becomes one published task rather than one asyncio task: the computed recipient data selects the queue, and Celery (or Kombu for raw AMQP) supplies the broker transport, publish retries and acknowledgement semantics. This variant trades latency and a broker dependency for durability and cross-process delivery, and it is the only form that keeps delivering when the producing process dies mid-fan-out. The in-process TaskGroup variant remains the right choice for local, low-latency fan-out.
variants.code_sketch:
for recipient in resolve_recipients(msg):          # recipient data -> queue name
    app.send_task(
        "notify.deliver",
        args=[msg.payload()],
        queue=recipient.queue,
        retry=True, retry_policy={"max_retries": 3},
    )   # no result backend => fire-and-forget, per-recipient outcome unknown
pitfalls: Tasks scheduled with eta/countdown live in worker memory until due and are redelivered when a Redis visibility timeout is exceeded - neither is a substitute for durable scheduling.
apply_async is fire-and-forget by design: without a result backend and correlation ids the fan-out has no per-recipient outcome at all.
Broker retries can publish a duplicate task; receivers must deduplicate (Idempotent Receiver) because the broker guarantees at-least-once, not exactly-once.
